notes.meaning: The Spirit of the Lord took hold of Ezekiel in a vision and placed him in the middle of a valley. The ground all around him was covered with human bones, lying unburied in the open air. This shocking sight pictured how completely ruined and helpless the people of Israel were during their exile.

The Lord led Ezekiel all around the valley so he could see the full picture. Countless bones were scattered across the open ground, and they were completely dry from long exposure to the sun and wind. Their dryness showed that death had ruled over them for a long time, leaving no natural hope of life.

God asked Ezekiel whether these dry bones could ever live again. Ezekiel knew that no human power could do such a thing, but he also knew that nothing is impossible for God. He humbly turned the question back to the Lord, trusting God's wisdom and power alone.

The Lord told Ezekiel to speak His word directly to the dry bones. Speaking to dead bones seemed useless to human eyes, but God's word carries the power to create and restore life. Ezekiel was told to summon the lifeless bones to hear the message of the Lord.

God promised that He would cause breath to enter into the bones so that they would come alive. Just as God breathed the breath of life into Adam at the beginning, only the living God could revive a dead nation. His promise guaranteed that life would return.

The Lord described how He would rebuild the bodies stage by stage, adding tendons, muscles, and skin over the bones. Finally, He would place His breath inside them so they would live. When this miracle took place, the people would know for certain that He is the true Lord.

Ezekiel obeyed and spoke the message God had given him. While he was speaking, a sudden rattling noise echoed across the valley as the bones began moving toward one another. Every bone traveled to its proper place, perfectly rejoining its matching bone.

As Ezekiel watched, tendons and flesh grew over the assembled skeletons, and skin covered them smoothly. The bodies were now fully formed and complete on the outside, yet they remained motionless corpses because there was no breath of life in them yet.

The Lord commanded Ezekiel to speak a second time, this time calling upon the breath or wind from all four directions to enter the slain bodies. Preaching God's word had rebuilt the bodies, but calling on God's Spirit was necessary to bring real life into them.

Ezekiel spoke as commanded, and the breath of life entered into the bodies. They came alive, stood up on their feet, and formed an immense army ready for service. God had turned a valley of dead bones into a living, upright host.

The Lord explained the meaning of the vision: the scattered bones represented the entire nation of Israel. The exiles were crying out that their bones were dried up, their hopes were dead, and they were completely cut off. God showed that He heard their cries of despair.

God told Ezekiel to bring good news to the hopeless people, calling them My people once again. Their exile felt like being locked in a grave, but the Lord promised to open those graves, raise them out of captivity, and bring them home to the land of Israel.

The people would truly know the Lord through this miraculous rescue. Only the Almighty God could bring a dead nation out of its grave of exile, and seeing His power and mercy would lead them to trust Him completely.

God promised to place His Holy Spirit within the people so that they would experience true spiritual life, and then He would settle them safely in their homeland. This confirmed that God was not only restoring their earthly home, but also renewing their hearts so they would love and follow Him.
The word of the Lord came to Ezekiel with a second instruction. This message followed right after the vision of the dry bones to reveal how God would unite His restored people.

God told Ezekiel to take two pieces of wood and write a name on each one. On the first stick he wrote for Judah and the Israelites with him, representing the southern kingdom. On the second stick he wrote for Joseph and the northern tribes led by Ephraim, representing the kingdom that broke away long before.

Ezekiel was told to hold the two pieces of wood together end to end in his hand so they appeared as one single stick. This visual sign demonstrated that God planned to heal the ancient division between the tribes and unite them into one family again.

God told Ezekiel that the people would watch him do this and ask him to explain what the two sticks meant. God often used object lessons through the prophets to awaken curiosity and prepare hearts to hear His word.

Ezekiel was to explain that God Himself would take the stick of Joseph and join it with the stick of Judah. Human rebellion had torn the nation apart centuries earlier, but the Lord promised to join them together into one stick in His own hand.

The prophet was commanded to keep the two joined sticks in his hand in plain sight of the onlookers while delivering the message. Holding the sticks before their eyes gave the people an unforgettable picture of God's promise of unity.

The Lord declared that He would gather the Israelites out from all the foreign nations where they had been scattered. He would collect them from every direction and guide them back into their own homeland.

God promised that once back in the land, the people would become a single united nation on the mountains of Israel. One king would rule over all of them, and they would never again be split into two rival kingdoms.

The Lord promised to rescue His people from the worship of idols and all their rebellious ways, washing away their guilt. Cleansed from their past sins, they would live in a renewed relationship where they would be His people and He would be their God.

God promised that His servant David would be king over them and serve as the single shepherd for the whole nation. Guided by this leader, the people would gladly walk in God's ways and keep His commands.

differ.view: The prophecy means that the literal, resurrected King David will rule over restored Israel on earth during the millennium.
David represents Jesus Christ, the promised Son of David and the Good Shepherd, who rules forever over His people.

notes.meaning: The people would live securely in the land given to Jacob, passing it down to their children and grandchildren through future generations. The promised ruler from David's line would serve as their prince forever, giving them lasting peace.

The Lord promised to establish an everlasting covenant of peace with them, blessing them and increasing their numbers. Most wonderfully, He promised to set His holy sanctuary in their midst forever, showing that He would never abandon them again.

God declared that His dwelling place would be right among His people, confirming the close bond between them. He would be their God, protecting and caring for them, and they would belong entirely to Him.

When the Lord sets His holy sanctuary among His people forever, the surrounding nations will see it and realize that the Lord Himself makes Israel holy. God's faithfulness in restoring and purifying His people would display His glory to the entire world.
